Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join. The CGT, a major labor union, backs the protests, calling for higher wages and pensions. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said hundreds of protest actions and more than 80 marches were expected nationwide.

articles.title: Trump insider who set up Katie Zacharia with secret ‘kill order’ revealed: report
articles.description: Katie Zacharia's brutal exit as President Donald Trump's press secretary didn't happen by accident, insiders say, pointing to a powerful figure pulling the strings. White House chief of staff Susie Wiles orchestrated the ouster of Zacharia, who lasted just five days on the job, The Daily Mail reported Friday. Wiles had reportedly been bypassed when the president plucked Zacharia, a 41-year-old former communications adviser at his media company, from relative obscurity last week. One senior Trump administration official told The Daily Mail that "Susie gave Fox News the kill order," while adding that Zacharia "was an obviously bad choice." That order, according to the report, set the stage for a live Thursday night interview in which Sean Hannity, whom Zacharia considered an ally, grilled her over her shaky debut briefing and her legal credentials. Trump had called her an attorney, but she never passed the bar exam. Zacharia told Hannity the result was "inconsequential" because she knew she would be living in China. The pressure continued Friday morning on "Fox & Friends," where co-host Lawrence Jones opened by asking whether she wished she had told the president about the bar exam. A second senior Trump official told The Daily Mail that someone at the White House "set her up," adding, "It only could have been Susie or the president himself." Fox News insiders rejected the "kill order" account, arguing Zacharia had sunk herself by the end of the Hannity segment. Zacharia did not respond to the outlet's requests for comment. White House communications director Steven Cheung announced Friday that Zacharia would move into a new role to be named later. Only days earlier, Cheung had brushed off reports of internal doubts about her as "trash." Trump, who hailed her first briefing as "excellent" on Tuesday, struck a gentle tone with reporters after their Friday meeting. "I want her to have a good life," he said. Behind closed doors, however, Politico reported that Trump told officials she "had no talent and shouldn't be on television." Wiles is now reportedly circling back to Scott Jennings, the Trump-friendly CNN contributor she favored before Zacharia was picked to replace Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August. A former Trump official confirmed to the outlet that Jennings is the frontrunner. Jennings did not comment.

articles.title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia roasted for only lasting 5 days on the job
articles.description: If you thought Anthony Scaramucci had an embarrassing run under President Donald Trump's leadership, he has nothing on Katie Zacharia. Scaramucci may have only served an 11-day stint as the White House Communications Director in 2017, but Zacharia beat that record as President Trump's press secretary. She was fired after just five days of her job, most of which were mired in controversy. According to a report by The New York Times, Trump let Zacharia go on Friday, October 16, after only starting her new job on Monday. While her rocky, 14-minute debut briefing raised immediate eyebrows, things quickly devolved. Her tenure came to a sudden halt after The Wall Street Journal revealed she had practiced law for years without actually passing the bar exam. After her first press briefing on Tuesday, journalists questioned Zacharia’s pedigree as a lawyer after learning she had failed the California bar exam. Zacharia later told Real America’s Voice host Jack Posobiec in an interview on October 15 that she had been advised to call herself a “lawyer” but “not an attorney at law.” This hair-splitting answer didn’t go over well with Sean Hannity, who pressed Zacharia about her legal background and got her to admit she failed the bar exam and never retook it. Her defense when she went back on Fox on Friday? “I’m being hired as White House press secretary and not White House counsel,” she said. Just hours after her Fox & Friends appearance, Trump encouraged her to quit, and The New York Times then reported she had been fired. Since the news broke, the internet has relentlessly roasted the now-former press secretary. People on social media are calling her five-day stint in the position “one half a Scaramucci” and joking that at least she has her career as an attorney to fall back on. California Governor Gavin Newsom’s office even posted a memorial for her short-lived career. Scaramucci got in on the zingers too, comparing Zacharia’s tenure to the lifespan of a head of lettuce, in reference to a 2022 internet challenge tested the theory that former British Prime Minister Liz Truss left office so quickly that a head of lettuce wouldn’t have time to wilt. Keep scrolling to see the funniest reactions!

articles.title: Trump DHS Is Building Deranged Case Against Ilhan Omar
articles.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin revealed Friday that the Trump administration is hoping to bring a criminal conspiracy case against Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar. Appearing on Real America’s Voice, Mullin discussed his agency’s plan to go after the Democratic lawmaker after her home in Washington was raided Monday, just three weeks before November’s midterm elections. The federal government is reportedly investigating how Omar got her citizenship after she arrived in the United States from Somalia as a child. “If someone comes in and claims—that fills out their paperwork illegally, and they claim that they are this person, and this is their background, and then underneath that individual, a lot of other people come in … then that can be considered a RICO case,” Mullin said. “There was a conspiracy to deceive the American government, and therefore everything else that came in with it could then for be looked at as the same case,” the secretary said. “Good thing about something like a case like that, is when it is a RICO case, that the statue of limitations on things, they don’t, they don’t apply. A few cases they do, but in most cases they don’t,” he added. The probe ostensibly centers on whether Omar’s father put her age as 17 rather than 18 on her citizenship application to allow her to qualify immediately for citizenship alongside his own application. In order to strip her American citizenship, the Department of Justice has to sue in federal court and prove that the person materially lied to get their status. It’s still unclear what, if any, evidence DHS has found to support this crusade against one of the president’s most outspoken critics. Mullin claimed that DHS “worked very closely with DOJ through the whole process.” So surely, he should know about one crucial section of the DOJ manual that bars federal prosecutors from timing any action, including investigative steps, criminal charges, or statements, for the purpose of undermining a candidate in an upcoming election. Mullin’s remarks came the same day that early voting began in Minnesota. If the Trump administration really wants to talk about a RICO case, then maybe we should discuss how President Donald Trump is weaponizing federal agencies to go after his critics? Or if we want to just stick with a classic, we can always revisit that pesky grand jury indictment Trump and his buddies received for their efforts to overturn the results of the 2024 presidential election.
